newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN TAILENDERS HOLD OUT SRI LANKA BOWLERS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN TAILENDERS HOLD OUT SRI LANKA BOWLERS.

text.p: Pakistan's lower order frustrated Sri Lanka's bowling attack as they carried their total to within 10 runs of a first innings lead on the third day of the first test on Monday.
Pakistan were 321 for seven at the close of the middle session with Saqlain Mushtaq still at the crease on 24 after holding out for nearly two hours. Mushtaq Ahmed was unbeaten on 18.
Asif Mujtaba was the only wicket to fall during the session which saw the addition of just 66 runs.
Mujtaba lobbed a return catch to off-spinner Muthiah Muralitharan after making 21 with the total on 298.
Mujtaba and Saqlain added 50 runs for the seventh wicket after Pakistan had lost three wickets for one run to Muralitharan in the morning session.

The only redeeming feature of the first session for Pakistan was Ijaz Ahmed's century. He was initially given out by umpire David Shepherd when he was on 98, but went on to complete his century after the decision was overturned by the third umpire.

Ijaz played a ball from Muralitharan to skipper Arjuna Ranatunga at short mid-wicket and set off for a single. Salim Malik responded but turned his back on the run which left both batsmen at the non-striker's end.
Shepherd gave Ijaz out and the batsman returned to the pavilion and was replaced by Inzamam-ul-Haq.
Inzamam was about to take guard when Shepherd, after advice from third umpire K.T. Francis, reversed his decision and recalled Ijaz, declaring Salim out instead.
A relieved Ijaz then went on to complete a well deserved century in 276 minutes off 204 balls with 11 fours.
He received a reprieve on 109 when substitute fielder Sajeeva de Silva missed a high catch at long-on off Kumar Dharmasena, but on 113 he became Muralitharan's third victim of the morning.
